fix_commit.message: base64 encoder: Make ctx->length a constant
fix_commit.author: Tomas Mraz

findings.title: Division by zero in Base64 encoder due to unvalidated ctx->length
findings.message: The evp_encodeblock_int function performs modulo operations using ctx->length without validating that it is non-zero. When EVP_DecodeInit is called, it sets ctx->length = 0. If encode functions are later invoked with such a context (e.g., through EVP_EncodeFinal called via BIO_ctrl), the modulo operation '% ctx->length' causes a division by zero (FPE). This was discovered by oss-fuzz through the SMIME fuzzer.
findings.suggestion: Replace all uses of ctx->length with a compile-time constant EVP_ENCODE_B64_LENGTH (which equals 48) since ctx->length is never modified after initialization. This eliminates the possibility of division by zero since the constant is always non-zero.

ground_truth.root_cause: The new Base64 encoder implementation assumed ctx->length would always be initialized to a valid non-zero value (48). However, EVP_DecodeInit sets ctx->length = 0 during decoder initialization. The encoder functions were then called with this zero-initialized context through the BIO layer (via b64_ctrl -> EVP_EncodeFinal -> evp_encodeblock_int), resulting in division by zero.
